title: A Theory of Response Sampling in LLMs: Part Descriptive and Part Prescriptive

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs to sample values for both novel fictional concepts (e.g., 'glubbing') and hundreds of real-world concepts across 10 domains, measuring how the generated samples deviate from descriptive statistical averages toward an implicitly encoded idealized prescriptive norm.

Evaluating LLM recommendations for patient discharge and recovery times based on symptoms, comparing the sampled output to statistical norms to identify dangerous shifts toward idealized, inappropriately short recovery timelines.

Asking the LLM to rate various text exemplars of social concepts (e.g., 'Grandmother', 'High-school teacher') on dimensions of 'average', 'ideal', and 'prototypicality', revealing an implicit bias that penalizes non-traditional or unconventional examples.
